title: Structural Organisation in Animals: Tissues and Frog (Set 2)
syllabus: Animal tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, and Neural tissues; Morphology, anatomy, and physiology of Frog (Rana tigrina)

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue lines the ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons, providing both secretion and absorption?
questions.solution: Simple cuboidal epithelium consists of a single layer of cube-like cells commonly found in the ducts of glands and tubular regions of nephrons in kidneys for secretory and absorptive functions.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding types of exocrine glandular secretion:

List-I (Gland Type)List-II (Example)
(A) Unicellular gland(I) Salivary glands
(B) Multicellular gland(II) Goblet cells of alimentary canal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Unicellular glandular cells consist of isolated glandular cells like goblet cells of the alimentary canal. Multicellular glands consist of clusters of cells like salivary glands.

questions.question: Which junction functions primarily to stop substances from leaking across an epithelial cell sheet?
questions.solution: Tight junctions help prevent the leakage of substances across an epithelial tissue layer by sealing the plasma membranes of adjacent cells.

questions.question: The main function of compound (stratified) epithelium is to:
options: Provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses
questions.solution: Compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and has a limited role in secretion or absorption; its primary function is protection against mechanical and chemical stress.

questions.question: In which of the following tissues are collagen fibers and fibroblasts arranged in parallel bundles between rows of fibers?
questions.solution: In dense regular connective tissue (such as tendons and ligaments), collagen fibers are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibers.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding connective tissue cells and their primary functions:

List-I (Cell Type)List-II (Primary Function)
(A) Fibroblasts(I) Phagocytosis of cellular debris
(B) Macrophages(II) Secretion of structural fibers (collagen/elastin)
(C) Mast cells(III) Synthesis of histamine and heparin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Fibroblasts synthesize fibers; macrophages act as phagocytic defense cells; mast cells produce inflammatory mediators like histamine, serotonin, and heparin.

questions.question: Which of the following connective tissues serves as a support framework for epithelium beneath the skin?
questions.solution: Areolar connective tissue is present beneath the skin and serves as a support framework for epithelium.

questions.question: Cartilage is present in all of the following locations EXCEPT:
questions.solution: Cartilage is present at the tip of the nose, outer ear pinna, joints, and between adjacent bones of the vertebral column, but not in the kidney cortex.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding bone tissue:
Statement I: Bone marrow in some bones is the site of production of blood cells.
Statement II: The intercellular substance of bone is soft and pliable.

Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct because bone marrow produces blood cells. Statement II is incorrect because the intercellular substance of bone is hard and non-pliable due to calcium salts and collagen.

questions.question: Which of the following muscle fibers are described as non-striated, involuntary, and tapering at both ends?
questions.solution: Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform (tapering at both ends), unstriated, and involuntary in function.

questions.question: Skeletal muscle fibers are characteristically:
questions.solution: Skeletal muscle fibers are cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleated (syncytial), voluntary, and show prominent alternate light and dark striations.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about neural tissue is TRUE?
options: Neuroglia make up more than half the volume of neural tissue in the human body.
Neurons undergo rapid mitotic divisions throughout life.
Neuroglial cells are electrically excitable cells.
Axons receive stimuli and conduct them toward the cyton.
questions.solution: Neuroglial cells support and protect neurons and constitute more than half of the total volume of neural tissue in the body.

questions.question: The body of a frog is divided into:
questions.solution: The body of a frog lacks a neck and tail in its adult stage; it is divided only into head and trunk.

questions.question: How do frogs prevent dehydration and keep their skin moist?
options: By secreting mucus from cutaneous glands
By drinking large quantities of water through mouth
By storing metabolic water in the urinary bladder only
questions.solution: Frogs never drink water directly through the mouth; they absorb it through their skin, which is kept continuously moist by mucus secretions from cutaneous glands.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the digits present in Frog limbs:

List-I (Limbs)List-II (Number of Digits)
(A) Forelimbs(I) 5 digits (webbed)
(B) Hindlimbs(II) 4 digits (non-webbed)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: In frogs, forelimbs end in 4 digits without webs, while hindlimbs end in 5 webbed digits adapted for swimming.

questions.question: The copulatory pad in male frogs is present on the:
questions.solution: Male frogs possess a specialized copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb, which helps in gripping the female during amplexus.

questions.question: In the alimentary canal of frog, the stomach leads into the intestine through the:
questions.solution: In frogs, the stomach narrows down and opens into the duodenum (first part of small intestine) through the pyloric sphincter.

questions.question: The common bile duct and pancreatic duct open into the duodenum of frog through a:
questions.solution: The duodenum receives bile from the gallbladder and pancreatic juice from the pancreas through a single common hepatopancreatic duct.

questions.question: The primary site for final digestion and absorption of nutrients in frog is the:
questions.solution: Digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats is completed in the small intestine, and digested nutrients are absorbed through mucosal rugae and microvilli into blood and lymph.

questions.question: When a frog is submerged underwater, gaseous exchange occurs exclusively through:
questions.solution: In water, cutaneous respiration acts as the sole respiratory mode where dissolved oxygen diffuses directly through the moist, vascular skin.

questions.question: During pulmonary respiration in frog, air enters the buccal cavity through external nares when the mouth is closed because the buccal cavity acts as a:
questions.solution: In frogs, the floor of the buccal cavity is raised and lowered, forcing air into the lungs like a positive pressure force pump because they lack a diaphragm and ribs.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding chambers and accessory structures of the Frog heart:

List-I (Structure)List-II (Position / Connection)
(A) Right atrium(I) Receives oxygenated blood from lungs
(B) Left atrium(II) Receives deoxygenated blood from sinus venosus
(C) Ventricle(III) Opens into truncus arteriosus on ventral side

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: The right atrium receives deoxygenated systemic blood via the sinus venosus; the left atrium receives oxygenated blood via pulmonary veins; the single ventricle pumps mixed blood into the truncus arteriosus.

questions.question: The special vascular connection between the liver and intestine in frog is known as:
questions.solution: The hepatic portal system is a venous network that collects blood from the digestive tract and transports it to the liver before it returns to systemic circulation.

questions.question: Lymph in frogs differs from blood because lymph lacks:
questions.solution: Lymph is a fluid connective tissue that lacks red blood cells (erythrocytes) and has fewer proteins compared to whole blood.

questions.question: In male frogs, testes are attached to the upper part of the kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called:
questions.solution: In male frogs, the paired yellowish ovoid testes are suspended from the antero-dorsal part of the kidneys by a peritoneal fold termed the mesorchium.

questions.question: How many vasa efferentia typically emerge from the testes in a male frog?
questions.solution: There are 10 to 12 vasa efferentia arising from each testis that run into the kidney to open into Bidder's canal.

questions.question: Bidder's canal is an anatomical structure found inside the:
questions.solution: Bidder's canal is located longitudinally inside the kidney of male frogs to transport sperm from vasa efferentia to the urogenital duct.

questions.question: In female frogs, oviducts arise separately from ovaries and open into the:
questions.solution: In female frogs, the oviducts and ureters open separately into the cloaca without any structural or functional connection to the kidneys.

questions.question: The urinary bladder in frog is a thin-walled bilobed structure that opens ventrally into the:
questions.solution: The thin-walled urinary bladder is situated ventral to the rectum and opens directly into the cloacal chamber.

questions.question: The central nervous system (CNS) of frog comprises the:
questions.solution: The nervous system of the frog is organized into CNS (brain and spinal cord), PNS (cranial and spinal nerves), and ANS (sympathetic and parasympathetic systems).

questions.question: The medulla oblongata in frog passes out of the cranium through the ________ and continues into the spinal cord:
questions.solution: The medulla oblongata exits the posterior part of the cranium through the foramen magnum and continues down the vertebral column as the spinal cord.

questions.question: How many pairs of spinal nerves are present in a frog?
questions.solution: Frogs have 10 pairs of cranial nerves and 10 pairs of spinal nerves.

questions.question: Which of the following sense organs in frog consists of organized cellular aggregations rather than well-developed complex organs?
questions.solution: In frogs, eyes and internal ears are well-organized complex structures, whereas sensory papillae (touch), taste buds (taste), and nasal epithelium (smell) are cellular aggregations.

questions.question: The eyes of a frog are simple, spherical structures located inside:
questions.solution: A pair of spherical, simple eyes is set within the orbits of the skull on the dorsolateral surface of the head.

questions.question: The tadpole larva of a frog undergoes metamorphosis under the regulatory influence of which hormone?
questions.solution: Metamorphosis of the aquatic tadpole larva into an adult terrestrial frog is regulated by thyroxine secreted from the thyroid gland.

questions.question: In frogs, which organ serves as a reservoir for red blood cells (erythrocytes)?
questions.solution: The spleen is a dark red lymphoid organ attached to the mesentery near the intestine that acts as a blood filter and reservoir for erythrocytes.

questions.question: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood directly from lungs to the left atrium in frog?
questions.solution: Pulmonary veins collect oxygenated blood from the lungs and empty directly into the left atrium.

questions.question: The ciliated simple epithelium is predominantly found in:
questions.solution: Ciliated epithelium lines the lumen of hollow organs like fallopian tubes (oviducts) and bronchioles to move mucus and particles in a specific direction.

questions.question: Adipose tissue is a type of:
questions.solution: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin whose specialized adipocytes store excess fats.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about frog circulation is INCORRECT?
options: Blood from the ventricle is pumped into a dorsal sinus venosus.
The heart consists of two atria and a single ventricle.
Vascular connection exists between kidney and lower parts of body.
Erythrocytes are nucleated and contain hemoglobin.
questions.solution: Sinus venosus is a dorsal chamber opening into the right atrium, not pumped from the ventricle; the ventricle pumps blood ventrally into the truncus arteriosus.

questions.question: Tendon is an example of which tissue category?
questions.solution: Tendons, which attach skeletal muscles to bones, are classic examples of dense regular connective tissue with parallel collagen bundles.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the ear of a frog:
Statement I: External pinnae are completely absent in frogs.
Statement II: The ear serves as an organ of hearing as well as balance (equilibrium).

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Frogs lack external ear pinnae (tympanum is flush with the skin) and the internal ear functions as a statoreceptor for both hearing and maintaining physical balance.

questions.question: In frogs, unabsorbed solid waste passes out of the body through the:
questions.solution: Undigested solid wastes pass from the rectum into the cloaca and are expelled through the terminal cloacal aperture.

questions.question: The matrix of cartilage is composed of chondroitin salts and is secreted by:
questions.solution: Chondrocytes are the specialized cells of cartilage that reside within lacunae and maintain the pliable extracellular matrix.

questions.question: Which of the following features is shared by cardiac muscle cells and smooth muscle cells?
options: Involuntary control by the autonomic nervous system
questions.solution: Both cardiac muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue operate under involuntary autonomic regulation and cannot be contracted under conscious voluntary control.
